Columns of C are independent, so callers may split C into strips.\ntemplate <size_t K, size_t W>\nstatic inline void kernelRowDep(unsigned int* C, unsigned int* P, const unsigned int* A,\n                                const size_t ld, const unsigned int kBase) {\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < K; ++k) {\n        const unsigned int kk = kBase + static_cast<unsigned int>(k);\n        alignas(64) unsigned int b[W];\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < W; ++j) b[j] = C[k * ld + j];\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < K; ++i) {\n            const unsigned int aik = A[i * ld + k];\n            unsigned int* cRow = C + i * ld;\n            unsigned int* pRow = P + i * ld;\n            #pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < W; ++j) {\n                const unsigned int nd = aik + b[j];\n                const bool lt = nd < cRow[j];\n                cRow[j] = lt ? nd : cRow[j];\n                pRow[j] = lt ? kk : pRow[j];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Pivot-column type: C (M x K) with A == C (columns k of C itself), B (K x K)\n// final pivot. Rows of C are independent, so callers may split C into row groups.\ntemplate <size_t M, size_t K>\nstatic inline void kernelColDep(unsigned int* C, unsigned int* P, const unsigned int* B,\n                                const size_t ld, const unsigned int kBase) {\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < M; ++i) {\n        alignas(64) unsigned int c[K];\n        alignas(64) unsigned int p[K];\n        unsigned int* cRow = C + i * ld;\n        unsigned int* pRow = P + i * ld;\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < K; ++j) { c[j] = cRow[j]; p[j] = pRow[j]; }\n        for (size_t k = 0; k < K; ++k) {\n            const unsigned int kk = kBase + static_cast<unsigned int>(k);\n            const unsigned int cik = c[k];\n            const unsigned int* bRow = B + k * ld;\n            #pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < K; ++j) {\n                const unsigned int nd = cik + bRow[j];\n                const bool lt = nd < c[j];\n                c[j] = lt ? nd : c[j];\n                p[j] = lt ? kk : p[j];\n            }\n        }\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < K; ++j) { cRow[j] = c[j]; pRow[j] = p[j]; }\n    }\n}\n\n// Classic in-place Floyd-Warshall on an S x S tile.\ntemplate <size_t S>\nstatic inline void kernelPivot(unsigned int* C, unsigned int* P,\n                               const size_t ld, const unsigned int kBase) {\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < S; ++k) {\n        const unsigned int kk = kBase + static_cast<unsigned int>(k);\n        alignas(64) unsigned int b[S];\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < S; ++j) b[j] = C[k * ld + j];\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < S; ++i) {\n            const unsigned int aik = C[i * ld + k];\n            unsigned int* cRow = C + i * ld;\n            unsigned int* pRow = P + i * ld;\n            #pragma omp simd\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < S; ++j) {\n                const unsigned int nd = aik + b[j];\n                const bool lt = nd < cRow[j];\n                cRow[j] = lt ? nd : cRow[j];\n                pRow[j] = lt ? kk : pRow[j];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Blocked Floyd-Warshall of one BS x BS pivot tile using SB x SB sub-tiles.\nstatic void pivotTile(unsigned int* C, unsigned int* P, const size_t ld, const unsigned int kBase) {\n    constexpr size_t ns = BS / SB;\n    for (size_t s = 0; s < ns; ++s) {\n        const unsigned int kb = kBase + static_cast<unsigned int>(s * SB);\n        unsigned int* Css = C + s * SB * ld + s * SB;\n        unsigned int* Pss = P + s * SB * ld + s * SB;\n        kernelPivot<SB>(Css, Pss, ld, kb);\n        for (size_t t = 0; t < ns; ++t) {\n            if (t == s) continue;\n            kernelRowDep<SB, SB>(C + s * SB * ld + t * SB, P + s * SB * ld + t * SB, Css, ld, kb);\n            kernelColDep<SB, SB>(C + t * SB * ld + s * SB, P + t * SB * ld + s * SB, Css, ld, kb);\n        }\n        for (size_t u = 0; u < ns; ++u) {\n            if (u == s) continue;\n            for (size_t t = 0; t < ns; ++t) {\n                if (t == s) continue;\n                kernelIndep<SB, SB, SB>(C + u * SB * ld + t * SB, P + u * SB * ld + t * SB,\n                                        C + u * SB * ld + s * SB, C + s * SB * ld + t * SB,\n                                        ld, kb);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nvoid floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, \n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path, \n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Blocked Floyd-Warshall. Row-major view: element (i, j) lives at\n    // idx2(j, i, n) = i * n + j. The matrix is padded to a multiple of BS with\n    // unreachable (INF) dummy nodes, which never improve any real path.\n    const size_t n = numNodes;\n    if (n == 0) return;\n    const size_t nb = (n + BS - 1) / BS;\n    const size_t N = nb * BS;\n\n    unsigned int* D = static_cast<unsigned int*>(std::aligned_alloc(64, N * N * sizeof(unsigned int)));\n    unsigned int* P = static_cast<unsigned int*>(std::aligned_alloc(64, N * N * sizeof(unsigned int)));\n\n    #pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        // Copy in (first touch distributed across threads)\n        #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {\n            unsigned int* dRow = D + i * N;\n            unsigned int* pRow = P + i * N;\n            if (i < n) {\n                std::memcpy(dRow, dist.data() + i * n, n * sizeof(unsigned int));\n                std::memcpy(pRow, path.data() + i * n, n * sizeof(unsigned int));\n                for (size_t j = n; j < N; ++j) { dRow[j] = INF; pRow[j] = 0; }\n            } else {\n                for (size_t j = 0; j < N; ++j) { dRow[j] = INF; pRow[j] = 0; }\n                dRow[i] = 0;\n            }\n        }\n\n        const size_t nOther = nb - 1;\n        constexpr size_t parts = BS / SB;\n        for (size_t kb = 0; kb < nb; ++kb) {\n            const unsigned int kBase = static_cast<unsigned int>(kb * BS);\n            unsigned int* Dkk = D + kb * BS * N + kb * BS;\n            unsigned int* Pkk = P + kb * BS * N + kb * BS;\n\n            // Phase 1: pivot tile\n            #pragma omp single\n            pivotTile(Dkk, Pkk, N, kBase);\n\n            // Phase 2: pivot row tiles (split into column strips) and pivot\n            // column tiles (split into row groups)\n            #pragma omp for schedule(dynamic, 1)\n            for (size_t t = 0; t < 2 * nOther * parts; ++t) {\n                const size_t part = t % parts;\n                const size_t tile = t / parts;\n                size_t o = tile % nOther;\n                if (o >= kb) ++o;\n                if (tile < nOther) {\n                    // Row tile (kb, o), columns [part*SB, (part+1)*SB)\n                    const size_t off = kb * BS * N + o * BS + part * SB;\n                    kernelRowDep<BS, SB>(D + off, P + off, Dkk, N, kBase);\n                } else {\n                    // Column tile (o, kb), rows [part*SB, (part+1)*SB)\n                    const size_t off = (o * BS + part * SB) * N + kb * BS;\n                    kernelColDep<SB, BS>(D + off, P + off, Dkk, N, kBase);\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Phase 3: all remaining tiles\n            #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n            for (size_t t = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n            std::memcpy(dist.data() + i * n, D + i * N, n * sizeof(unsigned int));\n            std::memcpy(path.data() + i * n, P + i * N, n * sizeof(unsigned int));\n        }\n    }\n\n    std::free(D);\n    std::free(P);\n}\n\n'''\nopen('floydwarshall.cpp','w').write(s[:a]+new+s[b:])\nEOF\ncp floydwarshall.cpp /tmp/fwo/fw/ && cd /tmp/fwo/fw && cmake --build build 2>&1 | grep -E \"warn|error\"; {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfiFVofqCDRD1rjb8uJqJ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've parallelized the Floyd-Warshall benchmark with OpenMP. On a 2×64-core EPYC 7763 (256 threads), the distance-matrix hash matches the original at every size I tried (n = 1, 100, 333, 1000, 1500, 2048, 4096), and `-v` validation passes at each size.\n\n| n | Original | Parallel |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1000 | 1144 ms | ~19 ms |\n| 2048 | 9383 ms | ~58 ms |\n| 4096 | 74567 ms | ~300 ms (~180 ms with `OMP_NUM_THREADS=128`) |\n| 8192 | not run | ~860–1000 ms (≈550–640 GOPS) |\n\nOther users were on the machine during testing (load average about 20–30), so timings varied by roughly ±20%.\n\n**What changed in `floydwarshall.cpp`:**\n- **Tiled algorithm:** the main loop is now a blocked (tiled) Floyd-Warshall with 128×128 tiles. Each round has three steps: the pivot tile on one thread, the tiles in the pivot's row and column in parallel, then all other tiles in parallel. All of it runs inside one OpenMP parallel region.\n- **Fast inner loops:** they are vectorized and keep partial results in registers. The pivot tile is processed in 32×32 pieces, and the pivot-row/column tiles are split into small strips so there are enough tasks to keep all threads busy.\n- **Padding:** the matrix is padded internally to a multiple of 128 with unreachable dummy nodes, so any `n` works. The padded matrix is spread across both CPU sockets' memory.\n- **Row-length padding:** each stored row is 16 elements longer than needed. Without this, rows of a tile collided in the same cache slots, and this change alone cut single-thread time at n=4096 from 13.4 s to 9.4 s.\n- **Thread cap:** the program never starts more threads than there are tiles to work on, which fixed a fixed ~25 ms overhead at small sizes.\n- **Path-matrix setup:** now parallel, and it produces the same values as the original loop.\n- The random graph setup stays sequential so the input data is identical.\n\n**`CMakeLists.txt`:** adds `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and links `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`. The executable name is unchanged.\n\n**Results and limitations:**\n- **Distance matrix:** identical to the original's.\n- **Path matrix:** each entry is still a valid intermediate node on a shortest path. But where two shortest paths tie, the tiled order can record a different node than the original loop would. The program never prints or checks this matrix.\n- **Thread placement:** the runtime's default placement isn't ideal here. Setting `OMP_PROC_BIND=close OMP_PLACES=threads` or `OMP_WAIT_POLICY=active` at run time took n=4096 from about 330 ms to about 150 ms. Requesting binding in the code itself made no reliable difference, so I left it to the environment.\n\n**Build note:** the source includes `../common/results_output.hpp`, which isn't in this workspace, so I built and tested in a scratch copy under `/tmp` next to a `common` directory I had available."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":363,"cache_read_input_tokens":51741,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":363},"output_tokens":7,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a9d3d4ad-91c7-427e-9671-7995f7ca41cf","uuid":"54f08fd8-ad66-499c-ab6c-d94b792e3999","timestamp":"2026-10-05T01:50:05.359Z","request_id":"req_011CfiFVoLyzRUdkXhPUyKr5"}
